title: feat(service-automation): a suspended run resumes on the flow version it started on
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01LjZwNRFiG2fkp8SNf6rHNx?thread=cmsg_01LjZwNRFiG2fkp8SNf6rHNx6LHkNZuGuGDkyTFjmHmjiD)_
Fixes #28405

Clause-②: yes (widening: a nullable `flow_checksum` column on `sys_automation_run`, the optional `SuspendedRun.flowChecksum`, and `AutomationEngine.setFlowHistorySource` with its exported `FlowHistorySource` type)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:挂起的运行(审批、屏幕等)在暂停时记下它所跑流程定义的内容校验和(`sys_automation_run.flow_checksum`,即 `sys_metadata_history` 存版本用的同一个 checksum);恢复时按这个校验和找回原定义继续跑,而不是跑名下当前注册的新定义。
- 为什么改:审批可能等好几天。期间流程被重新发布,原来的运行会被挪到新定义上,或者因为暂停的节点改名直接被判 `RUN_NOT_FOUND`。这是客户自定义流程(N-11、N-18)的前提。
- 风险与回滚:新列可空,老行读作“没有校验和”,恢复行为和以前一样;找不回原定义时退回当前定义并打 `warn`;元数据历史读不到时回答可重试的 `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`,运行保持暂停。回滚即 revert 本 PR,新列留着无人读。
- 先看:`packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts`(`resolveResumeTarget` 改成 async 及 `resumeInternal` 里的 `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` 分支)、`src/plugin.ts`(`flowHistoryReader`,经 `getByHash` 读历史)、`src/engine.ts`(`registerFlow` 记校验和、`recoverStoredFlow` / `heldFlowVersion`)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/flow-version-pinning.test.ts src/flow-version-pinning.integration.test.ts`,预期 8 个用例全绿,含 sqlite 文件上的重启用例。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

A suspended run now resumes on the flow body it started on, not on whatever is registered under its name at resume time.

- **New column `sys_automation_run.flow_checksum`** (`Field.text`, nullable, max 80, group Identity). It holds `hashSpec(body, 'flow')` of the body the run is executing, written on the paused row and, beside a consumed suspension, on the terminal row so a restore re-arms the pause pinned to it. `flow_version` stays the author's display integer. `SuspendedRun` gains the optional `flowChecksum`; the store maps it both ways (`readFlowChecksum`: absent or empty reads as "no identity").
- **The identity is computed at `registerFlow`** over the body exactly as handed over (`flow-identity.ts`), and kept per parsed body in a `WeakMap`. Every suspension site (`execute`, `executeWithoutRetry`, the resume's re-suspend) records the identity of the body that segment ran on.
- **`resolveResumeTarget` is now async** and takes an engine host instead of the bare `flows` map. It is still the one classification shared by the resume and the pre-flight `unresumableSuspensionCause` (card item 5). Order (card item 2): the armed definition when its identity matches; else `getByHash` through the new `setFlowHistorySource`; else a body this process registered under the name (from the engine's in-process version history, which is how a code-loaded body is found). New runs keep starting on the armed definition.
- **`getByHash` seam.** The plugin attaches `flowHistoryReader`, which builds a `SysMetadataRepository` over the `objectql` (or `data`) service at question time and calls `getByHash({ type: 'flow', name }, checksum)`. It is built here rather than asked of the protocol because the protocol keeps its repository private and exposes no read by checksum; the read is one system `findOne` on `sys_metadata_history`. No file outside `packages/services/service-automation/src/**` changed. A composition with no `sys_metadata_history` answers "not stored".
- **A history that cannot be read answers `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`** (already in `RETRYABLE_RESUME_REFUSAL_CODES`): the suspension is not consumed and the run stays parked, the same answer an unreadable suspended-run store gives. The pre-flight rejects in that case, as its contract already says for an unreadable store. An outage is never read as "not stored".
- **Unchanged on purpose.** A row with no recorded identity reads the armed definition, node checked (card item 3). A flow no longer registered at all is still `Flow '…' not found` even when pinned: it was withdrawn, not republished.
- **Item 4, decided on the card:** a pinned body recoverable nowhere (a code package upgraded under the run) resumes on the armed definition with its node checked, and the resume logs one `warn` naming the flow, its `flow_version` and the checksum it could not recover. The pre-flight only classifies and does not log.
- A stored body read back is parsed by the same `canonicalizeFlow` that `registerFlow` uses, with no arming and no registration checks. A body that no longer parses is treated as not recovered, with a `warn`.

## Tests

- `src/flow-version-pinning.test.ts` (engine + JSON-cloning store):
  - parked on v1, v2 renames the parked node: the pre-flight answers no cause and the resume finishes on v1 (not `RUN_NOT_FOUND`);
  - the row records `hashSpec(v1, 'flow')` beside the display version;
  - a body changed without a `version` bump is still pinned;
  - new runs after v2 run v2 while the old run finishes on v1;
  - a row with no identity keeps today's reading (armed body; node-gone cause with the same text from pre-flight and resume; no warn);
  - an unrecoverable pinned body warns once, naming version and checksum, and resumes on the armed definition;
  - after a restart, the pinned body is recovered through the history source; a history outage answers `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`, leaves the row parked, and the pre-flight rejects.
- `src/flow-version-pinning.integration.test.ts`: two process lifetimes over one sqlite file, real `saveMetaItem`, real `sys_metadata_history`, default durable store. It measures the card's assumption directly: the parked row's `flow_checksum` equals the `checksum` of the history row the save wrote for v1. After the restart (v2 armed, nothing in memory) the run finishes on v1, a row with its `flow_checksum` nulled gets the legacy `RUN_NOT_FOUND`, and a new run parks on v2's node.
- Re-judged pins (card: "re-judges `unresumable-suspension-cause.test.ts`"):
  - `unresumable-suspension-cause.test.ts`: the parked-node-edited case now finishes; its `RUN_NOT_FOUND` text is kept on a row with no identity.
  - `engine.test.ts` (Durable Suspend / Resume): the republish case now finishes; the `RUN_NOT_FOUND` case is kept for a truly unrecoverable body (flow withdrawn, then a different body registered, no history).
  - `resume-gone-suspension-settle.test.ts`: the settle-to-failed case is kept, its body made truly unrecoverable the same way.

## Acceptance notes

- The card's lookup order (armed, then `getByHash`, then an in-process body) is kept literally. The in-process body is read from the engine's existing per-name version history, so it is lost on restart and on `withdrawFlow`, as the card's "code-loaded body" case expects.
- Flow credentials (#20790) stay keyed by flow name, node id and key against the live flow. A run resumed on a pinned body reads the current credential at those positions. Noted, not changed.
- The dispatch asked for `pnpm lint`; the os-dev contract assigns repo-wide lint to CI. Both were run, see Verification.

## Verification

All readings at head `337e86f4` (branch base `a727ba26b`).

<details><summary>Package tests, typecheck and lint</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test && pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck` (typecheck includes `check:test-typecheck`): Test Files 246 passed (246), Tests 3115 passed (3115). Lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- Before the re-judge (at `0c739f57`) the same run was 2 failed / 3112 passed: the two older pins in `engine.test.ts` and `resume-gone-suspension-settle.test.ts` that asserted `RUN_NOT_FOUND` for a republish-dropped node. Both are re-judged as described under Tests.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, as the dispatch asked): exit 0. eslint `--no-inline-config` on the 13 changed `.ts` files: exit 0.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (each leg through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs; restored blob equals HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

Tests import `src/` relatively, so no dist rebuild sits between mutation and run. Each leg ran the two new files plus `unresumable-suspension-cause.test.ts` (15 tests).

- A1, the pin ignored in `resolveResumeTarget`: 7 failed (rename, unbumped edit, new-runs, unrecoverable-warn, history recovery, the re-judged probe, the sqlite restart).
- A2, the identity computed over `{ version }` only: 6 failed (unbumped edit, recorded checksum, and the four that compare against the body hash).
- A3, the store's paused-row read drops `flowChecksum`: 1 failed (the sqlite restart).
- A4, the plugin attaches no history reader: 1 failed (the sqlite restart).
- A5, a missing identity defaulted to a fake checksum: 1 failed (the legacy-row pin).
- A6, the unrecoverable `warn` skipped: 1 failed (the unrecoverable pin).
- A7, the recovered body re-armed under the flow name: 2 failed (new runs after v2, and the sqlite restart's new-run check).
- A8, a history outage read as "not stored": 1 failed (the outage pin).

</details>

<details><summary>Dispatch gates</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 62 families from 14 paths vs merge base `a727ba26b` (886 changed lines). Every command run with exits captured to disk before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: 62 derived, 61 run, 1 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun.

- NOT MEASURED (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, needs a full `pnpm build`): `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` first exited 3 on the shallow clone (pinned fixture commit missing). After `git fetch --unshallow origin main` it exits 0 (48 cases).
- Every other derived command exited 0, `pnpm check:type-check-debt` included.

</details>
